text.p: Medical Action Industries Inc intends to make an acquisition in the medical products industry with annual sales in the $10 million to $15 million range, the company's president said.
"We are going to do acquisitions, there are no ifs ands or buts about it," Paul Meringola said in a telephone interview.
Meringola wants to make Medical Action less dependent on the sale of sterile laparotomy sponges and sterile operating room towels.

The company, which is expected to report $45 million to $46 million in sales for the fiscal year ending March 1997, maintains about 70 percent of the domestic market in sterile laparotomy sponges and 50 percent of the domestic market for sterile towels.
Meringola expects earnings per share for the year ending March 1997 to be in the $0.11 to $0.13 range and $0.16 to $0.20 the following year.
Medical Action reported sales of $38.8 million in the year ended March 1996 and net income of $710,743, or $0.09 a share.

Medical Action's recent acquisitions, such as Lawson Mardon Medical Products 's sterilization repackaging business in 1996 and QuanTech in 1994, has expanded the company's markets to doctors offices instead of mostly operating rooms, Merigola said.
While the company intends to grow through acquisitions, Meringola will not make acquisitions that will dilute earnings per share.
"We're not going to do it (buy a company) unless it's accretive to earnings," he said.
